description: Figures the federal and state tax a 2026 or 2027 Roth conversion adds to the household's year (tax_year; 2027 on the IRS's published 2027 brackets, Rev. Proc. 2026-35, the state line on each state's 2026 rules, labelled), its share of the amount converted and the cost of the next $1,000; the room left in the current federal bracket and below the next IRMAA tier; and flags an IRMAA tier crossing (with the surcharge two years later, on the 2026 tiers), Social Security the conversion makes taxable (the tax torpedo) and a senior-deduction phase-out. Computed by QuantCalc's federal and state tax APIs, as the website's Roth conversion cost calculator; requires a connected QuantCalc PRO licence or Tax Season Pass, and without one returns no figures and names the free page. Not tax advice.

age.description: The age reached in the tax year (18-110).

conversion.description: The amount to convert from a traditional IRA to a Roth IRA in the tax year.

filing_status.description: Filing status: single, married filing jointly (mfj), married filing separately (mfs) or head of household (hoh).

ira_distributions.description: Other taxable IRA or 401(k) withdrawals (RMDs included). Default 0.

pension.description: Taxable pension and annuity income. Default 0.

social_security.description: Gross Social Security benefits of the household. Default 0.

spouse_age.description: Joint return only: the spouse's age reached in the tax year. Default the same as age, stated.

spouse_split.description: Joint return only: whose the IRA money, pension and conversion are on the state return: even (half each), filer or spouse. It can change the tax in the states that tax each spouse's own income; federal tax does not depend on it. Default even, stated in the result.

state.description: Optional: two-letter code of the state (or DC) for the state tax line. Absent: federal only.

tax_year.description: The tax year: 2026 (default) or 2027. 2027: the federal tax on the IRS's published 2027 amounts (Rev. Proc. 2026-35) and the amounts the law fixes; the state line on each state's 2026 rules (most states have not published 2027's), labelled as such; the IRMAA effect on the 2026 tiers (the later tiers are not published). Stated in the result.
